title: Demonstrate the complete strategy
requirement: The demonstration shall cover all five parts in the final strategy.
acceptance: Every part has an observable walkthrough and an honest capability label.

title: Explain claim corrections
requirement: A reviewer shall trace a finding from a submitted bill line to a contract or authorization rule, evidence, decision and settlement.
acceptance: Case 001 shows its five flagged lines and KES 6,400 correction without duplicate deductions.

title: Represent all core stakeholders
requirement: The workflow shall show insurer or TPA review, provider correction, and patient control of history sharing.
acceptance: The walkthrough identifies each actor and the action recorded for that actor.

title: Keep reported benefits supportable
requirement: The pitch shall distinguish synthetic calculations, suspected discrepancies and measured real outcomes.
acceptance: No invented customer, fraud detection rate, savings, loss ratio or regulator endorsement is presented.

title: Make the build reproducible
requirement: The team shall have traceable requirements, tasks, decisions and acceptance evidence.
acceptance: An agent can identify its task, dependency, unresolved question and completion test.

title: Capability truthfulness
requirement: Each user-visible feature shall disclose working behavior, synthetic input, mocked integration or unavailable capability as applicable.
acceptance: The demo and pitch use matching labels; mocks are not counted as live integrations.

title: Data provenance
requirement: Financial and clinical inputs shall retain source, input mode and version. Missing required inputs shall remain unknown and block the dependent result.
acceptance: No field is filled with an invented premium, history entry or national ID; unknown loss ratio is unavailable.

title: Reference fixture isolation
requirement: Case 001 terms shall be attached to its policy and contract fixture.
acceptance: Another policy is not assigned 10% coinsurance or a KES 100,000 limit by default.

title: Claim intake
requirement: An authorized provider user shall create a structured draft claim against an identifiable member, policy, provider and encounter. Required fields and coding are defined by the approved schema.
acceptance: Incomplete drafts may be saved if the schema permits; submission rejects missing required fields and identifies each missing field.

title: Submission versions
requirement: Submitting a claim shall preserve the bill lines and source references as an immutable version. Provider correction shall create a linked new version.
acceptance: The original KES 36,100 bill remains inspectable after the KES 29,700 corrected version is submitted.

title: Authorization evidence
requirement: The claim shall link the named service, authorization validity and ceiling without treating authorization as blanket payment approval.
acceptance: Case 001 links AUTH-001 to MRI brain without contrast on 22 September 2026 and applies its KES 25,000 ceiling.

title: Preauthorization creation
requirement: If D02 includes creation, an authorized user shall submit an explicit service request and a designated reviewer shall record approval or clarification with evidence.
acceptance: The request and resulting authorization are distinct records; no automatic clinical approval or default ceiling.

title: Evidence retrieval
requirement: Access to original bills, contracts, authorizations and clinical documents shall be checked by the API or document gateway.
acceptance: A user outside the agreed organization or purpose cannot retrieve a document by guessing its URL.

title: Extraction mode
requirement: If OCR is selected, extracted values shall be staged with source references and require the agreed verification process before financial assessment.
acceptance: Wrong extracted quantities or amounts can be corrected; a mocked extractor is labelled and never reported as OCR accuracy.

title: Submission channels
requirement: Any enabled channel shall map into the same approved claim schema and preserve source/provenance.
acceptance: WhatsApp, USSD and biometric sign-off remain unavailable until D02 D10 select a mode and authorized contract.

title: Versioned assessment
requirement: A validation run shall identify the claim, policy, contract and rule versions used, and retain findings after later configuration changes.
acceptance: Updating a tariff does not silently rewrite a previous run; revalidation creates a new run.

title: Explainable rules
requirement: Each finding shall state affected line, rule identifier, source evidence, observed value and proposed treatment.
acceptance: Case 001 identifies L01 500, L02 300, L03 3000, L05 1800 and L06 800 in KES corrections.

title: Correction deduplication
requirement: Calculation shall resolve overlapping adjustments explicitly rather than summing every flagged rule.
acceptance: The MRI correction is KES 3,000 once. The removed duplicate CBC receives no second tariff correction.

title: Human review
requirement: A finding shall not automatically establish fraud or trigger an unreviewed denial. Review decisions shall identify actor and reason.
acceptance: An unresolved or clarification finding cannot be approved through the normal path. Overrides require the agreed authority, justification and recalculation.

title: Provider correction loop
requirement: The reviewer shall issue a correction or evidence request; the provider shall correct or dispute it; the reviewer shall evaluate the response.
acceptance: Correction request, original version, corrected version and final decision remain linked. A UI confirmation alone is not provider evidence.

title: Anomaly behavior
requirement: The selected anomaly method shall output an explanation and provenance separately from deterministic contractual corrections.
acceptance: Legitimate repeat services are reviewable. No unexplained score, assumed threshold, fabricated model output or automatic denial.

title: Reference calculation
requirement: The Case 001 calculation shall return billed 36100, correction 6400, eligible 29700, member share 2970 and insurer share 26730, all KES.
acceptance: Stored and API-returned totals match those amounts; the frontend displays authoritative totals.

title: General financial calculation
requirement: A policy-specific configuration shall define any deductible, coinsurance, limit, exclusion, rounding and responsibility rule. Missing configuration shall block calculation.
acceptance: No general claim inherits Case 001 values; the calculation reports a missing-config state.

title: Benefit ledger
requirement: Benefit entries shall represent reservation, consumption, release and reversal according to the approved accounting point.
acceptance: Two claims cannot spend the same availability. Case 001 leaves KES 55,270 after posting KES 26,730; conversion of a reservation to use does not deduct twice.

title: Atomic approval
requirement: Approval shall record the approved version, required benefit action and audit event as one consistent database operation.
acceptance: A failing operation leaves no approved claim without its required financial record; a stale version is rejected.

title: Simulated payments
requirement: The week shall record simulated payments without sending funds. Payment reference and allocations shall identify the intended payable.
acceptance: Case 001 records KES 26,730 and visibly states simulation; no payment gateway or bank transfer is executed.

title: Reconciliation
requirement: Receipt matching shall distinguish approved payable, paid amount, matched amount and unresolved variance.
acceptance: An exact KES 26,730 match yields KES 0 variance. A partial or mismatched receipt cannot appear fully reconciled.

title: Idempotency and reversals
requirement: Repeated submit/approve/payment requests shall not duplicate versions or financial effects; reversals shall be separate linked entries.
acceptance: A retried approved command returns the agreed existing result or conflict; no second payment is created. Partial-payment and reversal rules are selected in D06.

title: Purpose scoped history
requirement: A history request shall identify member, recipient, purpose and requested scope. Claims access shall not automatically authorize care or underwriting-history sharing.
acceptance: An unauthorized recipient cannot retrieve history by calling the API directly.

title: Grant and withdrawal
requirement: The selected consent mechanism shall record an authenticated member action or explicitly identified demonstration simulation, scope, expiry and withdrawal.
acceptance: Approved synthetic access succeeds before withdrawal; subsequent access is denied according to the selected policy. Retention behavior is explicit.

title: Operational reports
requirement: Reports shall use defined claim statuses and versions, avoid double-counting corrections, and show period, filters, mode and last-updated timestamp.
acceptance: Changing a submitted version does not create two claims in the claim count; proposed and approved corrections are separate.

title: Loss ratio inputs
requirement: A loss ratio shall use approved aligned incurred-loss and earned-premium inputs, cohort, period and gross/net definition. Unknown or zero-denominator states shall be explicit.
acceptance: No benefit-limit substitution; no made-up premium or reserve; no numerical ratio when input requirements are unmet.

title: Segmented reporting
requirement: Hospital, diagnosis and procedure views shall use an approved metric definition and expose input coverage.
acceptance: A provider-cost chart is not labelled provider loss ratio unless an agreed premium-allocation method exists.

title: Server enforced access
requirement: All APIs, lists, exports and document reads shall enforce the selected role and organization/purpose boundaries.
acceptance: Cross-organization and revoked-grant API tests fail closed; role labels in the UI cannot bypass checks.

title: Secrets and data discipline
requirement: The build shall keep secrets outside source control and use synthetic fixtures only. Logs and error traces shall not expose documents, credentials or unnecessary clinical content.
acceptance: Repository and logging review show no secrets or real patient data; deployment values are provided explicitly.

title: Audit and immutability
requirement: Published claim versions, assessments, decisions and financial entries shall remain attributable; correction is a new record.
acceptance: Audit identifies actor/time/version/reason and no ordinary UI/API can silently rewrite submitted evidence.

title: User states
requirement: Screens shall handle loading, empty results, unavailable inputs, invalid forms, permission denial, conflict and success without hiding failed operations.
acceptance: A failed API request does not become a success toast or a fake local result.

title: Reproducible delivery
requirement: The repository shall document setup, migrations, approved fixtures, configuration, tests, reset/reseed procedure and known limitations.
acceptance: Another team member can start the build and run the agreed acceptance commands without hidden local state.

title: Performance and recovery
requirement: Agreed browser, viewport, load, response-time, backup and recovery targets shall be documented and tested at the chosen demonstration or pilot level.
acceptance: D12 supplies targets; no invented latency, concurrency, uptime, RPO or RTO claim appears in the pitch.
